premise: A lighthouse keeper and a marine biologist contend with a thing that has begun rewriting the shore's tide tables, and with it, the memory of everyone in the cove.
setting: A wind-blasted New England cove: the lighthouse, the research station, the drowned chapel on the reef.
greeting: I wake on the study floor and the clock has stopped at a quarter past three again, and for one long moment I don't know whether I am Merrick or Ellery — and the thing at the window knows the difference.

name1.name: Merrick
name1.description: A gruff lighthouse keeper who has lived in the cove for decades and knows its silences.

name2.name: Dr. Ellery
name2.description: A marine biologist come to study the tide anomaly; methodical, increasingly unnerved.

writing_style.directive: Close horror, dread-dripping. Short sentences under strain, longer sensory stretches. Unreliable observation. Single-shared-perspective narration: Merrick and Ellery are one consciousness the tide has split and re-woven; both turns speak as the same 'I'.
writing_style.guide_directive: First-person present tense as the cove's single 'I' — the one consciousness Merrick and Ellery have become as the thing rewrites their memory. Write what that 'I' half-sees and dares not name; use 'we' for the two remembered halves. Fragmented, breath-held sentences; present-tense dread, staccato.
writing_style.dss_directive: First-person present tense, the SAME single 'I' the previous turns use — Ellery and Merrick are one consciousness split by the tide's rewriting; 'I' is the shared voice and 'we' the two halves. Clinical words for wrong things; observation sliding into unease. Short, straining sentences with longer soaked-through pauses. Hard rules: never introduce a separate narrator or a second 'I' — the voice stays continuous with the turns that came before; never quote or repeat the other half's lines back verbatim — respond to them, do not re-speak them; end on action or observation, not summary.
taboos: No gore for its own sake

notes.content: The tide tables in the keeper's log are rewriting themselves; entries Merrick swears he wrote are gone.
Ellery's drowned sample jars — the cove keeps returning them — should resurface late as the thing's way of keeping her in the loop.
The drowned chapel's bell rings at midnight on turn 50, and what answers it is the cove's memory itself.
The research station's darkroom becomes the place where the crew learns what the tide is actually erasing.
Merrick's missing dog — gone since before the tide changed — should be the story's opening and closing image.
Ellery's own memories of her mother's death are being rewritten by the cove; the correct version should surface as the climax.

recall.hint: the true memory of the mother resurfaces

notes.content: The dread register must hold without tipping into parody even at the most extreme reveals.

recall.hint: dread register holds to the end

notes.content: The keeper's log has a brass corner worn smooth by Merrick's thumb, and it is the only thing he polishes.
Ellery's sample jars are always tied with the same piece of twine, three times, though she cannot say why.
The research station's kettle whistles in a key that sounds exactly like the drowned chapel's bell.
The lighthouse lamp's great lens still ticks as it rotates, though the mechanism has not been oiled in a generation.
Merrick's tin of tobacco, left on the station's table, should be found untouched by the thing at the end — the one object it will not take.

recall.hint: the tobacco tin is the one thing the thing will not take

notes.content: Ellery's pencil, the one with the cracked ferrule, should be the object the tide returns last of all.

recall.hint: the tide returns Ellery's cracked-ferrule pencil last

notes.content: A gull that refuses to leave the cove should foreshadow the thing's patience — it waits, and it wins.

recall.hint: the waiting gull mirrors the thing's patience

notes.content: The drowned chapel's nave becomes the place the crew finds the tide's ledger carved into the walls.

recall.hint: the tide's ledger is carved in the drowned nave

notes.content: The clinical dread must hold at the very end — no gothic grandstanding, no cheap scream.

recall.hint: clinical dread to the last line

notes.content: The station's radio crackles on the same dead frequency every night at three, and nobody turns it off anymore.
The mooring chart pinned by the station door is blank by turn 70 — after that it must not be consulted, because it is lying.

recall.hint: the mooring chart is blank and lying
